G1.rationale: The principal results are computed from GWAS summary statistics using the Q Trait function in the Genomic SEM R package, and the exact version, input data, and scripts are archived on Zenodo, so a third party can re-run the computation.

quotes.quote: we found evidence of heterogeneity in the associations between EA (Q Trait (2) = 36.75, P < 0.001; lSRMR = 0.13), cognitive performance (Q Trait (2) = 26.61, P < 0.001; lSRMR = 0.11) and the individual AD phenotypes

Table 1. Heterogeneity statistics and patterns of associations between case-control GWAS of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and proxy-phenotype GWAX of maternal and paternal history of AD in relation to 14 biobehavioral external correlates.

G2.rationale: The paper's stated priority is the application of the Q Trait function to AD and cognitive g. The first principal quantitative result reported is the Q Trait statistic for educational attainment in the AD analysis (Q Trait(2)=36.75), which is the first row of Table 1 and the first result in the Results section.

quotes.quote: the exact version of the Q Trait function used, along with input data and scripts, has been archived on Zenodo (DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17186083 )

G3.rationale: The Zenodo deposit contains LDSC_ADGWAX_QTRAIT.RData and LDSC_G_FACTOR_QTRAIT.RData, which are the LDSC-derived genetic covariance matrices (S and V) that serve as the analysis inputs for the Q Trait function. These are minimally processed inputs, not the outputs of the Q Trait analysis.

quotes.quote: A χ 2 difference test is used to compare the common and independent pathways models, as indicated by the Q Trait heterogeneity index, which follows a χ 2 distribution with K − 1 degrees of freedom (where K represents the number of indicator traits loading on the common factor).
Q Trait = χ Independ e n t pathways model 2 - χ Common pathway model 2 with degrees of freedom equal to (K − 1).

lSRMR = 1 K ∑ k = 1 K ( r G Residual , k ) 2 where K is the number of indicator traits that load on the common factor, and r g Residual , k corresponds with the residual genetic correlation for indicator k .

G4.rationale: The paper describes the Q Trait statistic as a chi-square difference test between common and independent pathways models, and the lSRMR as the root mean square of residual genetic correlations. The method is described well enough to implement without the original code.

method_quotes.quote: A χ 2 difference test is used to compare the common and independent pathways models, as indicated by the Q Trait heterogeneity index, which follows a χ 2 distribution with K − 1 degrees of freedom (where K represents the number of indicator traits loading on the common factor).
Q Trait = χ Independ e n t pathways model 2 - χ Common pathway model 2 with degrees of freedom equal to (K − 1).
The Q Trait function starts by fitting a genomic SEM common pathway model to estimate the regression coefficient relating the external correlate with the common factor ( Fig. 1 ).

specification.input_notes: The file LDSC_ADGWAX_QTRAIT.RData contains the LDSC-derived genetic covariance matrix (S) and sampling covariance matrix (V) for the AD factor and external correlates. The script run_analysis.R and the Q Trait function file QTrait.r are needed to reproduce the analysis. The deposit also includes LDSC_G_FACTOR_QTRAIT.RData for the cognitive g factor analysis, but the target is from the AD analysis.
